findings.comment: Moonlight tower presence within 100 feet of construction limits cannot be determined from submitted site plan documents; requires verification against City of Austin geospatial data
applicableAreas: Limits of construction; 100-foot radius from any moonlight tower or guy wires if present
findings.observation: No moonlight tower or guy wire locations are depicted on the site plan sheets examined (Sheets 1-11, 21, 31). Facts.md does not reference any moonlight towers on or adjacent to the property. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) and site plan (Sheet 9) do not indicate moonlight tower locations. The grouping guidance explicitly states: 'Moonlight tower presence cannot be verified from available documents' and notes: 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone—flag for human verification.' The City of Austin maintains geospatial data on moonlight tower locations, but this data is not provided in the submitted site plan documents or facts.md.
findings.reasoning: Code § 14-11-201 and UCM § 5.2.1 establish that activities within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its guy wires trigger special permitting (Moonlight Tower Construction Permit), enhanced insurance requirements ($500,000 minimum), and protective barriers. The applicability rule states: 'Only when moonlight tower or associated guy wires are within 100 feet of limits of construction.' The grouping guidance acknowledges that determination of moonlight tower proximity 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone' and instructs to 'flag for human verification.' The site plan documents do not show moonlight towers, and facts.md does not indicate their presence. Without access to the City's geospatial database of moonlight tower locations, it is not possible to determine from the submitted site plan materials whether a moonlight tower is within 100 feet of the 2.26-acre limits of construction.

findings.comment: Verify with City GIS or Austin Energy records whether any historic moonlight towers are located within 100 feet of the Valley View Townhomes construction site. If a moonlight tower is present within 100 feet, show its location and guy wires/posts on the plans and provide documentation of Special Moonlight Tower Construction Permit compliance (Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201).
findings.observation: The grouping guidance states: 'Note: Cannot be determined from plans alone—requires external location data. Flag for human verification if proximity uncertain.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704 in Council District 5. Austin maintains 17 historic moonlight towers throughout the city. The closest known moonlight tower locations would require City GIS lookup or Austin Energy records. The survey and plans do not indicate any moonlight tower presence within 100 feet of the construction area.
findings.reasoning: Moonlight tower locations are not defined in code and cannot be determined from plan review alone. This requires external City GIS or Austin Energy records verification. The grouping instructions state this item 'cannot be determined from plans alone.'

findings.comment: Moonlight tower proximity cannot be verified from submitted site plan documents. Requires verification using City of Austin geospatial moonlight tower location database to determine if a tower exists within 100 feet of the limits of construction.
applicableAreas: 100-foot radius around any existing moonlight tower or guy wires
findings.observation: The site plan documents, including the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) and all other sheets reviewed, do not identify or call out the location of any existing moonlight towers or associated guy wires on or within 100 feet of the property. The grouping instructions for this item explicitly note that moonlight tower locations 'requires geospatial data on moonlight tower locations not available from plans alone.' No geospatial analysis or moonlight tower proximity study is attached to or referenced in the site plan documents. The limits of construction are shown on the site plan, but without moonlight tower location data, the applicability of this requirement cannot be verified from the submitted site plan documents alone.
findings.reasoning: Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201 requires a moonlight tower construction permit when construction activities occur within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or associated guy wires. The requirement to include a plan note regarding removal and storage of moonlight towers during construction (EL-7.18) is triggered only when such a tower exists within 100 feet of the limits of construction. The submitted site plan documents do not contain sufficient information to determine whether a moonlight tower exists within the 100-foot proximity threshold. The City of Austin maintains geospatial data on moonlight tower locations that is not included in the site plan document set. This determination cannot be made from the plans alone and requires human verification using the City's moonlight tower inventory database.

findings.comment: Verify with City of Austin GIS or Austin Energy records whether a moonlight tower exists within 100 feet of the property. If yes, show guy wire locations and labels on plans, and provide documentation of required Moonlight Tower Construction Permit.
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not indicate the presence of a moonlight tower on or within 100 feet of the property. The grouping guidance notes: 'Moonlight tower locations are not defined in code and require verification with City GIS or Austin Energy records—this cannot be determined from plans alone unless the survey shows a moonlight tower.' The property location (3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704) would need to be cross-referenced with the City of Austin moonlight tower inventory.
findings.reasoning: Per Code of Ordinances § 14-11-201, construction within 100 feet of a moonlight tower or its guy wires requires special permits, protective barriers, and enhanced insurance. However, this information is not derivable from the submitted plans and requires external verification with City GIS or Austin Energy records. The grouping guidance explicitly states this 'cannot be determined from plans alone.'
